title: Membrane

reference.source: Reference 13: hand-inked cell print with a mint channel network, 850 × 1200 px JPEG scan
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Cells from a jittered lattice read through one warped distance field, so fill, keyline and gap come from one number; a channel field pushes the cells aside and takes a keyline of its own.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 850 × 1200 and every length scales with the canvas

cell.does: Lattice spacing of the seeds. The reference's gray cells have a median equivalent diameter of 87 px.

jitter.does: How far each seed leaves its lattice point. 0 is a tidy honeycomb.

vary.does: Per-seed weight: some cells grow at their neighbors' expense.

merge.does: Share of seeds dropped, so their neighbors grow into one large cell. The reference's largest cells are 4 times the median.

round.does: Smooth-min softness: how much each corner rounds and how big the black pocket at a junction gets.

warp.does: Low-frequency bend of the whole field; makes the walls wander.

green.does: Probability that a cell is filled green instead of gray. 30 of 73 in the reference.

gap.does: Black space between cell walls before the keylines are added.

keyline.does: Width of the black outline on every cell and channel edge. The reference's measures 4 px.

gain.does: Spread of the black into its neighbors after the scan blur, as wet ink does.

bleed.does: A faint, wide darkening of the fill beside every black line, 3 px out: the ink that wicked into the paper.

soft.does: Softness of every edge; the reference's black-to-gray edges run 2 px from 20 to 80 percent.

grain.does: Scanner grain in the fills: 3.5 levels on the gray, 5 on the green.

rivers.does: How many channels wander through the field.

channel.does: Width of the mint rivers: 1 is a 28 px median with a swell along the run.

wander.does: How much each channel swings side to side.

frame.does: Width of the mint border around the panel.

phase.does: Position along the loop. Slides a slow wave through the warp so the walls shift, and moves the swell along each channel.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: A wall: 4 px of black keyline on each side of a 6 px gap, all from one distance value.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: A channel: mint, 28 px median width, swelling along the run, with its own keyline where it passes a cell.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: A green cell: the fill is decided by hash, 41 percent of cells; its grain is 1.5 times the gray's.

pass_order: seeds on a 105 px lattice with 0.8 jitter, each with a size weight and a fill chosen by hash (41 % green)
one low-frequency warp of the coordinates for everything that follows

signed distance to the nearest cell wall: half the margin over the next seed, smooth-minned over the 3×3 neighborhood with a 22 px radius so corners round and junctions pocket; minus half the 6 px gap
channel field: distance to 3 wandering Catmull-Rom polylines minus a width that swells along the run; the channel pushes the cell distance back by one keyline
the panel edge does the same
cut: fill where the distance exceeds the 4 px keyline, channel where its field is negative, black elsewhere
scan blur 1.3 px on the masks, then a threshold shifted by the ink gain so black fattens; a 3.2 px bleed of the black into the fills; grain on the fills

measured.keyline_method: distance transform ridge of the black class

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Mint and gray palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: Cells and channels are generated, so the patch windows compare material on the plate's own cells: the flat patches were placed with search.py, the whole panel compares ink shares.

limits: Benchmark mean 0.96. The edge and junction tone histograms (0.80 to 0.85) miss on the mid-tone tail: the scan's black lines carry a 2 px ramp and a wider halo that the plate reproduces with a 1.3 px blur and a 3 px bleed, which leaves fewer pixels between 16 and 128 than the scan has.
Gray-fill autocorrelation 0.87: the scan grain correlates 0.81 at lag 1 and 0.49 at lag 2; a 2.8 px hashed grid resampled with Catmull-Rom falls off faster at lag 2.
Cells and channels are generated; the edge and junction patches were placed with search.py on the plate's own cells.
The reference's channels were drawn by hand and meet the frame at chosen points; the plate's wander from edge to edge, and one ends inside the panel with a taper.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
